newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Sime eyes 51 pct or more in Oriental.
newsitem.headline: Sime eyes 51 pct or more in Oriental.

text.p: Malaysian conglomerate Sime Darby Bhd said on Monday it plans to take up a 51 percent stake or more in Oriental Bank Bhd.
"We are pursuing a majority stake and that means 51 percent and above," Sime's chief executive officer, Nik Mohamed Yaacob told reporters.

He said Sime will not start negotiations until Malaysian Industrial Development Finance Bhd (MIDF), the 78.4 percent majority owner of Oriental Bank, gets approval from the central bank to open talks.
Nik Mohamed said Sime plans to merge Oriental Bank with its Sime Bank Bhd, which has just changed its name from United Malayan Banking Bhd (UMBC).

"This is in line with the government's encouragement for local banks to merge. We looked around at a few banks and decided that Oriental Bank was one of them. Fortunately it was approved," the chief executive said.
He said Sime wants to expand Sime Bank "so that it can face both domestic and foreign competition".
Nik Mohamed said financial services will be the future core activity of Sime Darby, now a widely diversified conglomerate.
"Financial services sector is the growth sector in Malaysia and is the key factor for the economy," he said.
Sime hopes to get the Oriental Bank talks settled "as soon as possible, hopefully within early next year", he said.
Sime said last week it has received approval from the central bank to negotiate with shareholders of the medium-sized Oriental Bank to acquire a majority equity interest.
The listing of Sime Bank is targeted for 1998, he said.
